claims.statement: This repository builds the Mintlify site docs.langchain.com from authored files in src/ into generated build/ output. DocumentationBuilder clears build/ and emits Python and JavaScript OSS variants, unversioned OpenWiki and Deep Agents Code content, LangSmith content, Managed Deep Agents variants, and shared files.

Local development requires running 'make install' to install dependencies and 'make dev' to start a development server at localhost:3000 that watches /src for changes and provides live preview through Mintlify.

`make test` runs pytest against tests/unit_tests with network sockets disabled except Unix sockets. Core CI runs on pushes to main, pull requests, and manual dispatch, and invokes that test target alongside separate lint, link, and cross-reference checks.

The development command runs an initial build unless --skip-build is supplied, starts a FileWatcher for src, and launches `mint dev --port 3000` with build as its working directory; it exits rather than continuing when the initial build fails.
src/docs.json is the Mintlify navigation and site-configuration source of truth, and contributors must update it when adding pages; generated build output must not be edited.
Most OSS documentation is generated into Python and JavaScript route variants, while OpenWiki and Deep Agents Code are unversioned output exceptions.
The project requires Python 3.13 or later; `make install` synchronizes all Python dependency groups, installs project npm dependencies, and installs the global Mintlify CLI.

Core CI regenerates `src/oss/python/integrations/providers/overview.mdx` with `pipeline/tools/partner_pkg_table.py` and rejects a resulting diff, so changes to that overview must be made through the generator or `packages.yml` and regeneration rather than by hand editing.

Runnable documentation sample source files under `src/code-samples/` are executed by `make test-code-samples`; `make code-snippets` extracts marked snippets into `src/code-samples-generated/` and generates imported MDX in `src/snippets/code-samples/`, so those outputs are not authored input.
`AGENTS.md` is the repository-wide authoring guide, while task-specific procedures are canonically stored in `.agents/skills/`; `make skills` links that tree into `.claude/skills/` for Claude Code.

The generated API reference at reference.langchain.com is built outside this repository, and the repository directs contributors to its reference-documentation issue template for problems with that site.

Integration discovery listings combine hosted-guide `integration:` frontmatter with external records in `scripts/data/integration_external_docs.yaml`; the refresh script provides an explicit documentation-URL validation mode before regeneration.

Source ownership and emitted route family are independent of Mintlify navigation: language-owned OSS subtrees emit only their matching route family, ordinary LangSmith content is unversioned, and Managed Deep Agents source files emit language-prefixed variants.

Shared unfenced OSS cross-references must resolve in both Python and JavaScript scopes, whereas language-specific API names can be placed in `:::python` or `:::js` blocks and are validated by the strict `make check-cross-refs` source gate.

`AGENTS.md` requires authors to work in manually authored `src/` content, use Markdown-free frontmatter descriptions and Tabler icons, add pages to `src/docs.json`, and test code examples before inclusion.

The navigation has separate agent-development-lifecycle and product/setup product menus, and menu labels do not reliably identify source ownership: Build mixes OSS and LangSmith content, Fleet is labeled No-code agents, and Deep Agents Code is a product/setup item.
Built link validation runs `make broken-links-with-anchors`, which builds first and checks links, anchors, and redirect destinations; the CI link workflow also runs `make check-openapi`.
Changes to scripts, workflows, Makefile targets, PR checks, scheduled jobs, or skills require the `docs-tooling-notion` documentation follow-up before a pull request is handed off.

The installed `docs` console script dispatches to `pipeline.cli:main` and provides development, build, move-with-link-update, and Markdown migration commands; Make development and build targets invoke the pipeline CLI.
In addition to reusable test, lint, and link workflows, core CI separately checks merge conflict markers, integration documentation URL schemes, and generated provider-overview drift.

The `docs-release-watch` Managed Deep Agent covers OpenWiki, Deep Agents Python, Deep Agents Code, and Deep Agents JS; for the newest eligible release published 7–30 days earlier, its product registry and matching skill drive source-and-docs research before one Linear DOC issue and one draft documentation PR are created per untracked user-facing feature.

Release-watch uses deployment-shared agent memory as an explicitly untrusted input boundary, keeps authority in tools rather than memory, and its documented safety model stores tracking URLs rather than credentials while requiring human review of draft-only pull requests.

The weekly Check integration repos workflow scans third-party `packages.yml` GitHub links, skips `langchain-ai/*`, writes evidence to the job summary, and opens or appends to a standing draft PR only when the scan changes files.

When a third-party integration GitHub repository is unavailable, the repository-health scanner may repair a confirmed third-party GitHub rename or permanent external-docs redirect, retains live GitLab or partner-documentation alternatives for attention, and fully delists only packages with no live VCS or partner-docs alternative.

The daily LangSmith OpenAPI refresh runs `scripts/process_langsmith_openapi.py --write` and reuses a standing `chore/refresh-langsmith-openapi` PR; its generated platform specification is `src/langsmith/langsmith-platform-openapi.json`, with fleet and internal endpoints filtered for public documentation.

The PR-to-Linear synchronization workflow runs only for same-repository pull requests on selected lifecycle events, has read-only GitHub permissions, skips successfully without `LINEAR_API_KEY`, and passes PR metadata through environment variables to the sync script before writing its JSON result to the job summary.

For a PR using the recognized `Closes DOC-N` convention, the Linear sync script maps draft, ready, merged, and unmerged-closed PRs to a preferred Linear state with a state-type fallback; it avoids an already-correct update but exits unsuccessfully if a linked issue's team has no suitable target state.
